subject: "Perhaps it is in basepairs?" warning, but no marker positions given in cross file

messages.author: 299eaf97b0ef4f53
messages.subject: "Perhaps it is in basepairs?" warning, but no marker positions given in cross file
parts:
Dear r/qtl community,

I have a SNP markers with physical positions based on a high quality, chromosome scale reference genome. I am using a RIL (F8) mapping population, of which one of the parents are the same genotype as the reference genome. 

From reading earlier posts, I believe it is better to have positions in cM for linkage mapping. When I input the cross file (csv) I give no positional information (i.e. formatted exactly the same as "mapthis" example data, row 1=marker ID, row 2= "1", row 3 onward= genotype data), however I still get the warning:

Warning messages:
1: In summary.cross(cross) : Strange genotype pattern.
2: In summary.cross(cross) :
  Some chromosomes > 1000 cM in length; there may be a problem with the genetic map.
  (Perhaps it is in basepairs?)

(I am just concerned with warning 2 - I know to use convert2riself() to solve warning 1). 

I know posts say to ignore it, but later on when I get to forming linkage groups (page 20 of the Genetic Map Construction with R/qtl tutorial) something strange happens when I try to order the markers. 
After orderMarkers() and pull.map(), I get strange cM positions (a linkage group expected to be 250 cM based on many other linkage maps is only 82 cM. 
The mapping generated the 9 linkage groups I expected, with correct markers in correct group. 

Can anyone help? I have some experience with QTL mapping, however I have never had to construct the linkage map, so your wisdom would be much appreciated.
Instead of doing all this, as I am confident with the physical positions could I just convert Mbp > cM?

Thanks in advance,
Annabelle

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] "Perhaps it is in basepairs?" warning, but no marker positions given in cross file
parts:
R/qtl requires positions, and so if you don’t provide them, it fills them in with a dummy set. If you have a lot of markers, this will lead to the warning about chromosomes being surprisingly long.

It shouldn’t affect the later map construction, and I’ve never seen a problem where linkage maps were smaller than expected. 

But if you have a high-quality physical map, I would use that for marker order and not use formLinkageGroups() or orderMarkers(). And if you also have an idea of the chromosomes’ cM length, I would use that to convert Mbp to approximate cM. 

I would generally prefer to re-estimate the genetic map (that is, re-estimate the inter-marker distances) before QTL mapping, but it depends on the size of your mapping population and the density of markers. If the markers are very dense, the genetic map doesn’t matter too much. And if the population is rather small, the estimated map won’t be very good.

karl
